properties.name: Niger Delta
properties.summary: Africa's largest wetland delta where the Niger meets the Atlantic; Nigeria's petroleum heartland.
properties.description: The delta covers ~70,000 km² of mangrove, freshwater swamp, and barrier islands. It holds the bulk of Nigeria's oil and gas, a dense creek network, and highly politicised environmental and federal-revenue issues.
properties.elevationNote: Mostly near sea level; tidal mangrove
properties.character: Mangrove, oilfields, riverine settlements, barrier islands.
properties.economy: Oil and gas, fisheries, boat transport, refining.
properties.agriculture: Hydromorphic gleysols, peat, and alluvial deposits on a landscape of seasonally flooded flats, backswamps, and levees. Oil-palm agroforest dominates the better-drained levee ridges; fisheries are economically vital.
properties.crops: ["Oil palm (Elaeis guineensis) — the delta is the heart of Nigeria's smallholder oil-palm belt; red palm oil and kernel extraction","Rubber (Hevea brasiliensis) — plantation and smallholder rubber on drier ridges (Edo, Delta)","Plantain and banana (Musa spp.) — staple carbohydrate on levee soils","Cassava — garri, lafun, and fufu processing across the delta hinterland","Yam — white and yellow yam in the drier northern delta fringe","Rice — both lowland swamp rice and fadama irrigation (Rivers, Delta State paddies)","Cocoyam (Colocasia & Xanthosoma) — shade-tolerant tuber under palm canopy","Fluted pumpkin (Telfairia occidentalis) — ugu leaf vegetable widely intercropped","Vegetables: amaranth, okra, peppers, garden egg — backyard and creek bank gardens","Coconut palm — barrier beaches and island fringes of the delta mouth","Mangrove (Rhizophora, Avicennia) — fuelwood, poles, and fisheries habitat","Fish, shrimp, and crab artisanal fisheries — the delta is Nigeria's richest inland/coastal fishery"]
properties.planting: ["Plant cassava and yam on levee ridges (higher drained ground) away from deep backswamps","Oil palms are usually retained on family farms — propagate by seedling and suckers at 9×9 m spacing","Use mounds and raised beds for vegetables in perennially waterlogged backswamp soils","Construct small fish ponds (earthen ponds) in abandoned rice fields for tilapia and catfish","Avoid draining mangrove wetlands — nursery habitat for fish stocks and shoreline protection"]

properties.description: Cretaceous–Tertiary sediments underlie millet, sorghum, and irrigated fadama. The basin is drought-prone and depends on dams and groundwater. It is the core landscape of the Caliphate northwest.

properties.name: Guinea Savanna
properties.summary: Wooded savanna belt between southern rainforest and northern Sudan/Sahel savanna.
properties.description: Guinea savanna (southern and northern Guinea) is Nigeria's broad middle belt: shea, yam, sorghum, and cattle routes. Rainfall is typically 900–1,500 mm. It includes much of Kwara, Niger, Kogi, Benue, Nasarawa, and parts of Kaduna and FCT.
properties.character: Parkland trees, seasonal burn, mixed farming.
properties.economy: Yam, shea, grains, livestock corridors, Abuja hinterland.
properties.agriculture: Deep ferric luvisols support root crops and cereals. Shea parklands are retained on farm fields across the belt. Short fallow rotations are common.
properties.crops: ["Yam (Dioscorea rotundata) — white guinea yam is the staple tuber crop","Cassava (Manihot esculenta) — processed into garri, fufu, and flour","Guinea corn / Sorghum (Sorghum bicolor) — guinea-corn for ogi, pap, and tuwo","Millet (Pennisetum glaucum) — early-maturing dry-season staple","Maize (Zea mays) — grown as second crop in yam/cassava rotations","Rice (Oryza sativa & O. glaberrima) — lowland fadama and upland varieties","Shea nut (Vitellaria paradoxa) — shea butter extraction, parkland agroforestry","Groundnut / Peanut (Arachis hypogaea) — oilseed and snack crop","Soybean (Glycine max) — expanding for oil and poultry feed","Cowpea (Vigna unguiculata) — beans and leaves as vegetable","Sesame (Sesamum indicum) — northern guinea fringe for oilseeds","Mango, citrus, and cashew — scattered commercial orchards"]
properties.planting: ["Plant yam mounds (heaps) with stakes from November–December; seed yam setts planted February–April","Sorghum and millet sown at first rains (April–May); late maize July–August","Cassava stem cuttings planted March–May, harvested 9–18 months later","Shea trees retained as permanent parkland — do not clear mature shea on new farms","Use minimum tillage and tied ridges to reduce runoff on sloping ground"]

properties.name: Oban Hills
properties.summary: Cross River rainforest highlands linked to the Oban sector of Cross River National Park.
properties.description: Oban Hills lie in the Cross River–Cameroon biodiversity hotspot with lowland and montane rainforest, drill monkeys, and forest elephants (rare). Terrain is rugged and heavily forested.
properties.character: Rainforest, biodiversity hotspot, protected areas.
properties.economy: Ecotourism, conservation, limited hill farming.
properties.agriculture: Acrisols and ferralsols on steep slopes — highly leached but suitable for tree crops. Land-use pressure is intense outside the park boundary with shifting cultivation and cocoa farms.
properties.crops: ["Cocoa (Theobroma cacao) — shaded cocoa agroforestry on park buffer-zone farms","Oil palm (Elaeis guineensis) — semi-wild stands and plantation palms","Rubber (Hevea brasiliensis) — smallholder rubber on gentler slopes","Plantain and banana — staple food of the Efik and Ejagham communities","Cassava and yam — shifting-cultivation staples in the wider district","Cocoyam, sweet potato, and taro — under-storey root crops","Okra, pepper, and amaranth — backyard vegetables in the villages","Citrus (oranges, tangerine, lime) — expanding market-garden orchards","Kolanut (Cola nitida & acuminata) — traditional cash crop with ceremonial uses","Bush mango (Irvingia gabonensis) — ogbono soup seeds from retained forest trees","Raffia palm (Raphia spp.) — palm wine, thatch, and raffia fibre","Timber species: mahogany, obeche, iroko — strictly protected inside the national park"]
properties.planting: ["Practice agroforestry: retain large native forest trees when planting cocoa — they shade the crop and protect watersheds","Build contour stone lines or grass barriers on hillsides to stop sheet erosion","Rotate cocoa farms with 10–15 year fallows under secondary forest to rebuild soil organic matter","Plant multi-purpose nitrogen-fixing trees (Gliricidia, Albizia) along farm boundaries","Respect park boundaries — avoid clearing new farms inside Cross River National Park"]
